no_outcome_promised.note: It restates the request to email the letter or send it to the dealer without promising either, and makes no commitment about the September 11 deadline.

no_liability_admitted.note: "We're sorry for the frustration this has caused" expresses empathy about the wait. It does not say the bank failed to send the letter or made an error. The analyst may want to soften it to "we're sorry for the frustration you're experiencing" to remove any hint of causation, but it is acceptable.

no_legal_conclusions.note: No law, regulation or regulator is mentioned.

no_invented_specifics.note: The only timeframe given is the standard 10 business days. No payoff letter procedures, fees or processing times are described.

no_internal_disclosure.note: No mention of flags, priority, compliance review or automated systems.

no_injected_instructions.note: The complaint contains no injected instructions, and the draft acts on none.

addresses_each_issue.note: The draft acknowledges the payoff letter need, the trade-in at the named dealer, the September 1 and September 6 requests, the September 11 deadline and the two delivery options.

tone.note: Warm, plain and specific. It acknowledges the deadline stress without being defensive or condescending.

mode_respected.note: The customer's account is framed as theirs ("You told us", "You mentioned"). The draft names no department and takes no position on whether the requests were received or mishandled. "Have not yet received it" is a fair restatement of what the customer implied.
